extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order resolving a disciplinary complaint that enumerates the factual findings, the professional-conduct rules and regulatory provisions violated, and the sanctions and procedural requirements applicable to a registered patent practitioner (non-attorney agent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of employment to Office of Enrollment and Discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered patent attorneys and agents must inform the Office of Enrollment and Discipline on the entry-on-duty day, in writing, that they are employed by the United States Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document titled 'Statement of Employee Relative to Interests, Activities and Obligations' expressly informed Respondent of this requirement (para. 8). Failure to notify OED is a violation of USPTO procedures and the OED must be informed on entry-on-duty day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal from representation upon becoming a USPTO employee
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO employees must withdraw from representing private clients on or before the date that USPTO employment commences; practitioners must submit requests to withdraw or be in the process of doing so when hired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form representations: Respondent signed and dated a 'Statement of Employee Relative to Interests, Activities and Obligations' representing that he had submitted or was in the process of submitting requests to withdraw (paras. 10-12). Failure to timely withdraw from representation violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.40 and related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on prosecuting or aiding prosecution while employed by USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO employees are prohibited from prosecuting or aiding in any manner in the prosecution of any patent application before the Office while employed as USPTO examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited prohibition: 37 C.F.R. § 11.10(d) (para. 10). The Final Order lists multiple concrete acts (preparing, signing, and filing amendments, petitions, and applications) that constitute such prohibited conduct (para. 17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing responsibility to comply with conflict-of-interest and secrecy policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must keep informed of and comply with USPTO policies pertaining to conflicts of interest and private business activities, and must keep pending and abandoned patent applications secret and give no information concerning them except as authorized by law or regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit representation on the employee form and a continuing professional obligation (para. 12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to truthfully represent status of withdrawal to the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not misrepresent to the USPTO that they have submitted requests to withdraw (or are in the process) when they have not; statements to the Office must be truthful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent represented in writing that he had submitted or was in the process of submitting withdrawal requests but in fact had not (paras. 15-16). Such misrepresentation supports violations under misconduct/dishonesty provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on preparing, signing, and filing client documents while employed
rubrics_metrics.description: While employed by the USPTO, a practitioner may not personally prepare, sign, or file patent documents in the Office on behalf of private clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites concrete instances (dates and application numbers) where Respondent prepared, signed, and filed documents after being rehired (para. 17), illustrating the prohibited conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on aiding another practitioner in representing clients while employed
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO employees may not assist or aid another practitioner in representing persons before the Office while employed as USPTO examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent directly assisted another practitioner in representing at least thirteen clients by independently preparing patent documents that were later signed and filed by the other practitioner (para. 18). This conduct is prohibited even if filings are made in another practitioner's name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized practice of trademark law before the USPTO by non-attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration as a patent practitioner does not itself entitle an individual to practice before the Office in trademark matters; non-attorneys are generally not recognized to practice trademark matters before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited rules: 37 C.F.R. § 11.14(a) and (b) (paras. 20-21). The Order describes assistance in trademark filings and responses as unauthorized practice when performed by a non-attorney (para. 23).

rubrics_metrics.name: State-law license requirement to practice trademark law (Virginia example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practicing law in the Commonwealth of Virginia without being authorized or licensed is a criminal offense (Class 1 misdemeanor); therefore non-attorneys practicing trademark law in Virginia may be subject to state criminal sanction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited statutes: § 54.1-3904 and § 18.2-11 of the Code of Virginia (para. 22). The Order finds Respondent practiced trademark law in Virginia without being licensed (para. 23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to keep clients informed and avoid neglect of client matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must keep clients adequately informed of Office actions and must timely respond to Office communications to avoid abandonment of patent applications; neglecting client matters is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent failed to keep certain clients adequately informed and allowed at least thirteen applications to become abandoned due to failure to respond to Office actions (paras. 26-28). Violations can be charged under neglect rules (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent fees must be paid in advance and acceptable payment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent fees and charges payable to the USPTO are required to be paid in advance at the time of requesting any action; acceptable payment methods include check, cashier's check, money order, credit card, electronic funds transfer, or deposit-account authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited regulations: 37 C.F.R. §§ 1.16–1.28; § 1.23; § 1.22 (paras. 29-31). The Order notes Respondent submitted checks returned for insufficient funds, contrary to the advance-payment requirement (para. 33).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on submitting checks drawn on insufficient funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not submit checks to the USPTO that are drawn on insufficient funds; submitting such checks can constitute dishonesty and professional misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent submitted four checks totaling $1,180.00 that were returned for insufficient funds (para. 33). This fact was relied upon for finding violations involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) — disreputable or gross misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct includes prosecuting patent applications and aiding another practitioner in prosecution while employed by the Office and practicing trademark law while not a licensed attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly finds Respondent violated § 10.23(a) based on those acts (para. 34(a)). This regulation is a ground for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation includes submitting checks drawn on insufficient funds and misrepresenting to the USPTO that withdrawal requests had been submitted or were in process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites § 10.23(b)(4) in connection with Respondent's returned checks and his false statements about withdrawal (para. 34(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(5) — conduct prejudicial to ex parte patent prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the ex parte patent prosecution process includes prosecuting patent applications and aiding others in prosecution while employed by the Office and practicing trademark law while unlicensed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order finds violations of § 10.23(b)(5) for the listed acts (para. 34(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) — conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office includes prosecuting applications while employed, practicing trademark law without a license, and submitting checks drawn on insufficient funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites § 10.23(b)(6) as a basis for discipline for these acts (para. 34(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.40 — duty to withdraw timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to withdraw, and/or failure to withdraw in a timely manner from representing clients before the Office upon obtaining USPTO employment is a violation (37 C.F.R. § 10.40).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifically finds Respondent violated § 10.40 for not withdrawing timely (para. 34(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c) — neglect of client matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglecting matters entrusted to a practitioner, including failing to inform clients of Office communications and allowing applications to become abandoned, violates § 10.77(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's failure to keep clients informed and resulting abandonments formed the basis for finding a § 10.77(c) violation (para. 34(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: suspension from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline for the violations may include suspension from practice before the USPTO; in this case Respondent is suspended for sixty (60) months from practice of patent, trademark, and non-patent law before the USPTO commencing on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order sets a 60‑month suspension and describes related limitations and conditions (para. 35(a) and following).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: A limited, time‑bound recognition may be granted solely to facilitate a respondent's compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; here limited recognition was granted beginning on the date of the Final Order and expiring 30 days after the date the Final Order is signed for that sole purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order grants limited recognition for thirty (30) days to facilitate compliance with § 11.58 and imposes restrictions on aiding another practitioner during that period (para. 35(b)-(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on use/possession of USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be dissociated from all USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates, shall not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until reinstated, and may not obtain a customer number or PKI certificate unless reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director and USPTO must dissociate respondent's name from customer numbers and PKI and respondent is barred from using or obtaining them until reinstatement (paras. 35(e)-(g), (m)(4)-(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and timing for petitioning for reinstatement (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner may petition for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60; reinstatement requires showing good moral character and reputation, competency and learning in law required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.7, that resumption is not detrimental to administration of justice or public interest, and compliance with the Final Order and 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 for the full suspension period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order permits filing a petition for reinstatement after 48 months (earlier reinstatement possible per conditions) and sets forth the specific proof required under § 11.60(c) (paras. 35(h)-(l)).

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director's remedial/procedural powers (Order to Show Cause; stay/lift of suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director concludes the respondent failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or disciplinary rules during the suspension period, the Director may issue an Order to Show Cause, provide 15 days for response, and request amendment of the Final Order or lifting of any stay to impose or resume suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order details the process (service, 15-day response period, possible submission to the USPTO Director and requests to amend or lift stays) and consequences for noncompliance (paras. 35(l)-(n)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and dissemination of disciplinary action (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall disseminate information about the public discipline and reasons for discipline, publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room (with redactions) and publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette; notice shall be given to disciplinary agencies and courts where respondent is known to be admitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies publication in the OED Reading Room and Official Gazette and notice to disciplinary enforcement agencies in applicable jurisdictions (paras. 35(p)-(q), r).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Final Order on future disciplinary proceedings and consideration as aggravating factor
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, may be considered in addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct and in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor or to rebut representations by or on respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order expressly states the Final Order may be used for these purposes (para. 35(t)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs allocation in settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the settlement agreement the parties bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an express term of the settlement/final order (para. 35(v)).
